comments: Child is correcting the assignment of items to people in response to MOT's question 'für wen is(t) das?'
'alle' in 'alle raus' is used as a quantifier meaning 'all/everyone', not as a negation meaning 'all gone'.
Child rejects mother's proposed action/interpretation ('I should drive?') to replace it with a modified plan involving the rabbit and stroller.
Child says 'nein da' after mother's 'prima', likely vetoing the current placement or directing attention to a different spot.
Child vetoes the mother's proposed way of lying down ('noch mal so?'), replacing it with a different manner.
Child uses a negative directive ('hol... nicht hier ab') to block or direct the mother's action regarding the stool.
Child remarks that the object is gone/absent following a question about its location (line 118397).
Child corrects the target of the action (showing the car) after the adult points out the mama is not there.
Child opposes Thorsten's claim to the Flipper ('ich krieg(e) den Flipper') in a dispute over toys, as evidenced by subsequent 'es geht nicht' and 'gib'.
Child resists Opa's request to 'komm mal hier' (line 126723).
Child denies the mother's question "is der für n Papi?" by asserting ownership ("mein deld").
Child answers a factual question about who is receiving the money (line 216960).
Child rejects the grandmother's statement that they must move over (line 217357).
Child answers 'no' to mother's question about whether they no longer want to paint; likely denying the mother's premise.
Child denies the mother's claim that she has poop in her pants (line 250007).
Child reports that items do not fit, which is a factual claim about a property; see Example T.
Child reports that a toy piece does not fit into the car ('geht nicht rein'), which is a report of a failed attempt/property.
Child resists the action of putting on shoes in the context of a discussion about buying new ones.
Child answers Mother's question "is(t) da ein Spiegel?" by stating there is no mirror.
Child reports that the toy phone does not turn on/work, following 'das is(t) kaputt'.
Child contradicts caregiver's claim that it is 'schon fertig' (line 281157).
Child remarks on the absence of the lid, echoing the mother's statement in line 281766/281770.
Child contradicts mother's claim that the animal is 'erst gebor(e)n' (line 282477).
Child opposes the dog having a ball in its mouth after Mother's observation in line 282611.
Child makes a factual claim about the mouse's inability to eat the snail.
Child states they do not know the animal in the book in response to the mother's prompt.
'alle' is used as a quantifier meaning 'all of them' (confirmed by GIS: 'du willst alles haben?'), not as a negation meaning 'all gone'.
Child reports a failed attempt to make something work/fit, repeating the sentiment from line 282972.
Child reports that a piece does not fit during play; factual report of a failed attempt.
Child expresses lack of desire for the object they were struggling with, functioning as a rejection of the item/activity.
Child denies the mother's assumption about their desire to play ('du möchtest noch eben spielen, ja?'), confirmed by the mother's surprised uptake 'auch nich(t)?'.
Child expresses refusal of an item ('will das nisch') during play.
Child expresses a lack of desire to continue building, rejecting the activity.
Child answers mother's question 'what do you want to do?' by stating they want to do nothing; repetition of the first 'nichts' in the utterance.
Child refuses the mother's directive to tidy up the railway ('einräum(e)n').
Child reports that the toy train does not work/fit while tidying up; a report of failed attempt is Denial (cf. Example T).
Child reports that something 'doesn't work/fit' while tidying up the train; similar to Example T.
Child is pretending to be on the phone; 'nee' followed by 'hier sind keiner da' (nobody is here) indicates the absence of the expected interlocutor.
Child remarks that there is nothing inside the container, following Mother's comment "alles leer" (everything is empty).
Child refuses the mother's request to tidy up (line 356487).
Child vetoes a proposed placement and suggests an alternative ('der soll da dran').
Child denies the caregiver's claim that she is also a sheep ('du bist auch ein Schaf').
